subject: Post-call: inference topology, isolation and burst profile

Subject: Post-call: inference topology, isolation and burst profile

Hi Alice / Bob — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned next steps and can scope a dedicated capacity proposal. If anything below looks off, flag it and I’ll update.

Summary of customer pain points (as discussed)
- Latency spikes during peak hours (user-facing inference for search and alerts).
- Unpredictable token cost from heavy batch jobs and periodic model retrains.
- Regulatory constraint: ability to isolate PHI-containing workloads and provide audit logs for a SOC2-type review.

Goals / success criteria
- 99.9% production availability for the user-facing endpoint during business hours (08:00–20:00 PT).
- Sub-120ms p95 latency target for simple chat prompts; p99 under 300ms if possible.
- Deterministic isolation for PHI traffic with separate compute pool and KMS integration.
- A staged ramp: pilot (2–4 weeks) → canary (1 month) → full reserve (quarterly commitment).

Workload profile you shared
- Peak concurrent requests: ~180 simultaneous sessions (mainly short prompts, avg 60 tokens).
- Background batch generation windows: nightly bulk jobs (2–3 hours) that can tolerate higher latency but must not impact the user pool.
- Average daily tokens: ~60M; peak day up to 120M.

Initial proposal hypotheses (for sizing & isolation)
- Dedicated pool with tenant isolation: 4-6 A100-class GPUs for user-facing pool (continuous batching, low-latency).
- Separate burst pool for batch/retains with preemptible capacity and a routing policy to protect the user-facing SLA.
- KV/prefix caching for the most common prompts to lower per-token cost and reduce p95.

Attachments: I’ve included a quick calc (orion_capacity_quickcalc.xlsx) and a short ops playbook we typically use for pilot-onboarding (redwood-dedicated-playbook.pdf).

Next steps (action items)
1) Alice: confirm the 180 concurrent sessions number and whether sessions originate from a single region (expected: us-west).
2) Bob: share any compliance checklist items required for KMS/HSM integration and retention windows.
3) Ben/Engineers: we’ll sketch a candidate sizing and a short runbook for pilot isolation.
4) Schedule a 60–90 minute technical workshop next week to walk through mapping sample traffic to pool sizes and test scripts.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm availability.

Thanks — K

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap, that matches our notes. A few clarifications and one constraint: 

Clarifications
- 180 concurrent sessions is our conservative estimate; we typically see 120–150 under normal load and spikes to ~180 across US-West and US-East (traffic is still mostly west).
- The nightly batch window is flexible — we can shift it to off-peak if that helps with isolation.

Compliance constraint
- We need separate key material for PHI traffic and 7-year retention for audit logs for the parts of the pipeline that touch patient identifiers. We can share a simplified checklist off this thread.

SLA ask
- We’re targeting 99.9% monthly availability for the user endpoints; we’d like to see how Redwood maps that into a proposed committed pool and what fallback policies look like if capacity is constrained.

We’re available for a technical workshop next Thursday afternoon (Jul 24) or Friday morning (Jul 25) PT. Would prefer a working session with networking and a short ops demo.

Alice

Kim — quick technical notes to feed into the sizing doc before the workshop. Putting these here so Alice and Bob can see and comment.

Notes
- Model choices: for user-facing low-latency we should prioritize an LLM variant that supports int8 quant and has a short KV cache line for dialogue (e.g., rdx-3.7-q8 or an equivalent open model). That reduces GPU footprint and improves p95.
- Pool sizing: estimate 4 x A100-80GB for predictable 120ms p95 at 180 concurrent sessions with batching tuned to 50–100ms windows. We can start pilot on 2 GPUs with load-gen to validate assumptions.
- Isolation: implement a dedicated VPC endpoint + separate pool label (phi-isolated). KMS integration will need key rotation docs but is standard (we have HSM connectors).
- Burst handling: recommend a throttled routing policy that redirects non-prod batch jobs to a burst pool (preemptible) with autoscaling capped to protect the user pool.

Open technical questions for workshop
- Do you have a preferred model family (we can test both open 3B/7B variants and a 13B if you want quality-first)?
- Expected max sequence length for the bulk jobs (this affects memory and cache).

I’ll turn these into a short slide for the workshop.

-Ben
